::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 9th 1877  
**Manuscript:** MS Harry Ransom Humanities Research Center,  University of Texas
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)

I am very sorry this sad check has fallen on all the bright hopes.[^1] I remember [Mrs Keble](people/person_795.qmd) saying, when my [brother](people/person_1624.qmd) lost his [first](people/person_1632.qmd), how often it happens that the first fruits of a family are thus consecrated and taken, and become in time a happy remembrance.

[May](people/person_351.qmd) has been hoping that [Minny](people/person_927.qmd)’s baby may come today on its [great grandfather](people/person_344.qmd)’s birthday, I wonder if it will. Poor [Katie Lloyd](people/person_887.qmd) is at Ramsgate, very lame.[^2]

I have a nice set of Will stories, some very funny and some very melancholy.[^3]

Your affectionate
C.M. Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY commiserates on the death of Thomas Drake Coleridge (18 Feb-2 July 1877), eldest son of Christabel Coleridge’s brother Ernest Hartley Coleridge (1846-1920).
[^2]: May was Mary Frances Keble Coleridge (1824-1898), daughter of Sir John Taylor Coleridge (9 July 1790-1876). Her niece Mary (Mackarness) Coleridge, who was married to Bernard Coleridge, was expecting a baby,  [Geoffrey Duke Coleridge](people/person_338.qmd), 3rd Lord Coleridge  (23 July 1877–1955).   Katie (Johns) Lloyd, was the former Gosling, who had married in 1873 the Rev. John Henry Lloyd, curate of Wormleighton.
[^3]: The Christmas 1877 number of *MP* consisted of stories on the theme 'Will'.
